text:
marcus: Quick license sanity check before we push Velvet-14B (our 4-bit quant experiments) into qa-stage. Model card: https://huggingface.co/velvet/velvet-14b — license shows CC-BY-NC-4.0. Question: can we run this on Hosted API (paid customers), Dedicated, or include a quantized variant in Private deployments? Also: are quantized weights treated as a redistribution/derivative that needs permission?

anya: Planning int4 runs this afternoon on a 2k prompt subset. Collecting generation diffs vs Oak-13B baseline. Will keep model weights local to dev hosts unless legal says otherwise.

oliver: Two short practical asks: 1) If the license is NC, does Dedicated (reserved capacity customers pay) count as commercial? 2) For Private (customer VPC/on-prem), if we ship a pre-quantized artifact to a customer, is that redistribution?

legal-ops: Short answer: CC BY-NC 4.0 == non-commercial only. Clarifications: Hosted API used to serve paying customers = commercial => not allowed. Dedicated where customers pay Redwood for capacity is also commercial. Private on-prem where the customer pulls artifacts from us is redistribution and therefore also not allowed unless we have a commercial grant. Quantized weights are generally treated as a derivative work (transforming the weights) — so quantized artifacts also fall under the model license. Attribution requirement still applies. I've opened COM-4789 to track outreach to the model authors.

sophia: :thinking_face: So internal evals and non-user-facing research is OK? We should record that all evals were non-public and tag logs for audit.

legal-ops: Correct — internal research/eval that is not part of a paid product is typically allowed under CC BY-NC, provided attribution is kept. But we must not distribute the model or quantized artifacts outside the company or to paying customers without a commercial license. Also: if we add prompts or fine-tuning, that can create further derivative issues — escalate if we go down that path.

sre-bot: compliance-ticket CREATED: COM-4789 (contact model authors for commercial license + confirm derivative/redistribution rules). Owner: legal-ops. Link: https://redwood-internal/tickets/COM-4789

marcus: Ok — pausing Hosted + Dedicated onboarding. Anya: run the int4 evals but do not sync quant artifacts to S3 or any shared bucket. Oliver: can you draft a fallback plan using Apache-2.0 alternatives (Oak-13B or Redwood-curated oak-small) for customers who need commercial-friendly models?

anya: Will do. I'll upload evaluation reports (metrics, example regressions, A/B diffs) to the evals repo but will exclude any saved quantized checkpoints.

legal-ops: Two further notes to record here: 1) If the model author offers a dual/commercial license, we need the license text and a signed agreement before we enable serving or redistribution. 2) Attribution: every end-customer-facing UI or docs must show the model name and license (example: "Velvet-14B — CC BY-NC 4.0") and include the link to the original model card.

oliver: :eyes: I'll draft a one-pager FAQ for sales/solutions explaining what we can and can't do with NC models and propose Apache2 alternatives.

marcus: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after COM-4789 updates or if the authors respond.
